hints.title: Core Idea
hints.text: With n <= 100, we can check all pairs of houses (i, j) with 1 <= i < j <= n.

hints.title: Key Observation
hints.text: The shortest path between house i and j is the minimum of direct line distance j - i and shortcut paths through x and y.

hints.title: Algorithmic Steps
hints.text: Distance is min(j - i, abs(i - x) + 1 + abs(j - y), abs(i - y) + 1 + abs(j - x)). Increment the count for this distance by 2 for both directions.

hints.title: Implementation

complexity.notes: Pairwise shortest path evaluation via direct formula.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Full all-pairs BFS takes O(n * (V + E)) = O(n^2) which is fine for n <= 100, but closed-form distance avoids BFS overhead.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(n) space for frequency array of distances.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Compute shortest path between pairs considering alternative route through shortcut.
